issue.title: Performance JSON parser accepts malformed suffixes
issue.promotion_reason: current contained failing evidence is repeatable or deterministically sufficient and satisfies the frozen plan

root_cause_group.claim: The JSON performance parser accepts malformed trailing bytes after a valid envelope.

theories.claim: The JSON performance output parser accepts malformed trailing data after an otherwise valid envelope.
theories.basis: The parser's second Decode rejects trailing content only when it returns nil, while the governed requirements require product-owned strict parsing and drift-sensitive output identity (qa-v1-block-dbf7e69765ab615487ff3a15, qa-v1-block-ce45392d2ebc036986b89d13).
theories.confirmation_condition: A line containing the required marker, one valid matching JSON envelope, and malformed non-whitespace trailing bytes is parsed successfully instead of being rejected.
theories.refutation_condition: The parser rejects every non-whitespace token after the first JSON value, including malformed trailing bytes that cause the second Decode call to return a syntax error rather than nil.
theories.inconclusive_condition: The omitted implementation differs materially from the cited changed hunk or another validated layer rejects such output before it can qualify a sample.
theories.safe_evidence_strategy: Exercise the existing parser test surface with a valid matching envelope followed by malformed trailing text; no subprocess or repository mutation is required.

evidence.summary: After decoding the envelope, parsePerformanceJSONValue reports trailing data only when decoder.Decode(&struct{}{}) returns nil. A syntax error from malformed trailing JSON is ignored before the envelope is accepted.
The cited parser tests cover duplicate envelopes and truncation but not a valid envelope followed by malformed trailing bytes.

After decoding the envelope, parsePerformanceJSONValue reports trailing data only when decoder.Decode(&struct{}{}) returns nil. A syntax error from malformed trailing JSON is ignored before the envelope is accepted.
The cited parser tests cover duplicate envelopes and truncation but not a valid envelope followed by malformed trailing bytes.
